sentences.text: Kerberosaurus was a saurolophine duckbill dinosaur living in Russia during the Upper Cretaceous period.
This extinct ornithopod hadrosaur is known only as the species Kerberosaurus manakini.
Scientists identify it by narrow frontals, a unique braincase shape, and a distinct separation between the bone around the nostrils and the surrounding bone.
The animal could reach a length of about 8 meters (26 feet).
Researchers Yuri Bolotsky and the Amur Complex Integrated Research Institute found a large bonebed containing these fossils in 1984.
This large herbivore likely fed on plants using complex dental batteries.
The genus belongs to the family Hadrosauridae and the subfamily Saurolophinae.
Cladistic analysis places Kerberosaurus as the sister taxon to the genera Saurolophus and Prosaurolophus.
The fossil record spans the Maastrichtian stage from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
In 2014, Xing et al. proposed that Kundurosaurus nagornyi is a junior synonym of Kerberosaurus manakini based on shared skeletal characters and occurrence in the same formation.
